# moodle-cli 0.8.1

Sign-in no longer depends on the CLI being able to read your browser's cookie store.

That store is unreadable in more places than it looks: macOS keeps it behind Full Disk
Access, which is granted to your terminal application rather than to the CLI; Chrome's
Safe Storage keychain prompt can block indefinitely; Windows app-bound encryption and
sandboxed agent terminals fail outright. Previously `moodle auth login` read a denied
store as "no session yet" and fell into a 120-second poll that could never succeed.

Three paths now cover it:

- **Browser sign-in over CDP.** `moodle auth login` launches a Chromium the CLI owns and
  reads the session over the DevTools pipe, instead of opening your system browser and
  waiting for a cookie to appear on disk.
- **Paste login.** `moodle auth login --paste` takes the cookie directly. The prompt does
  not echo and the value never reaches argv or shell history. Any paste carrying
  `MoodleSession` works, including a Network tab `Copy as cURL`, so you do not have to dig
  five panels deep for an HttpOnly value.
- **Browserless renewal.** Where the site enables the mobile web service, login captures a
  durable token and later commands mint a fresh cookie from it — no browser, no disk
  access. Support is detected from the site's public config and cached per instance, so a
  site without it is never probed twice. `moodle auth keepalive` uses the same path, which
  is what lets a background job renew unattended.

## Fixes

A denied cookie store is now detected by probing the store files directly and fails
immediately with the Full Disk Access hint, the exact paths, and the name of the terminal
application that needs the grant. Diagnostics list only stores that could have held a
session instead of four "database not found" lines for browsers you do not have.

Errors report the fault in front of them. A transport failure says so, with the host and
whether it timed out, rather than surfacing as "fetch failed" or sending you to log in
again. A failed login no longer deletes the cached session it was trying to replace.
`moodle doctor` exits non-zero when a check fails, and stops suggesting `auth login` when
the store it just checked is unreadable.

The CDP transport is bounded throughout: every request times out, `Browser.close`
escalates to SIGKILL, browsers are terminated even when the pipe errors, and a finished
login exits at once instead of lingering about 15 seconds. The paste prompt keeps a
multi-line paste whole. Mobile-token renewal rejects an anonymous login page that carries
a sesskey instead of caching it as a valid session, and a token that can never mint one is
refreshed rather than carried forward.

## Upgrade

```bash
npm install -g moodle-cli@0.8.1
```

No configuration or cache format changes. Existing sessions keep working; the next login
on a supported site adds the mobile token automatically.
